title: dedicated-autoscaler-backpressure-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler backpressure handling and utilization reporting: smoother token-bucket smoothing, new backpressure metrics, and improved throughput guarantees. Non-breaking operational change requiring config rollout.
description: Context: Customers running large Dedicated fleets observed transient request queueing and oscillation during cluster rebalancing and burst periods. Current token-bucket smoothing is too aggressive for low-utilization fleets and lacks visibility into backpressure events. Motivation: Reduce visible latency spikes, avoid over-provisioning from reactive scale-ups, and provide operators with clear utilization and backpressure signals for SLOs and automated runbooks. What this PR does: 1) Implements a two-tier token-bucket smoothing algorithm that decouples short-term burst allowance from long-term throughput guarantees; 2) Adds explicit backpressure state machine to the autoscaler (OK/THROTTLING/BACKPRESSURE) with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping; 3) Emits new observability metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.backpressure_events, dedicated.autoscaler.tokenbucket_fill_ratio, dedicated.autoscaler.shortburst_tokens, dedicated.autoscaler.longterm_tokens, and dedicated.fleet.throughput_guarantee_delta; 4) Improves utilization reporting by tagging utilization samples with bucket_state and scale_decision_reason; 5) Adds a config knob (autoscaler.burst_smoothing.window_ms, autoscaler.burst_smoothing.long_window_ms, autoscaler.backpressure.hysteresis_ms, autoscaler.throughput.guarantee_margin_pct) with sensible defaults to enable per-customer tuning; 6) Integrates a canary rollout in the operator to progressively enable backpressure for fleets above a threshold. Migration/Config: Defaults preserve prior behavior for fleets without explicit config. Environments: tested on local canary (k8s kind), staging dedicated fleets, and a small production canary (10 fleets) prior to wide rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9876) - [x] Unit tests for token-bucket smoothing - [x] Integration test for backpressure state transitions - [x] Metrics emitted and recorded in staging - [x] Dashboard updates (observability-pack) - [x] Canary rollout plan validated in staging - [x] Documentation update for config knobs Changes summary: commits: see commits list. Key files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go: new two-tier smoothing implementation and unit tests - pkg/autoscaler/backpressure.go: backpressure state machine and decision logic - pkg/metrics/emitters.go: new metric names and tagging support - deploy/operator/patches/autoscaler-config.yaml: new config knobs and defaults - observability-pack/dashboards/dedicated-autoscaler.json: dashboard updates - integration-tests/autoscaler_backpressure_test.go: E2E tests for state transitions - cmd/operator/rollout.go: canary rollout integration - docs/operations/autoscaler.md: documentation updates Performance/behavior notes: In staging we saw a 28% reduction in short-lived scale-ups and a 12% reduction in tail latency p99 during burst events for the tested workloads. Backpressure events correlate with sustained queue depth > 3s and are surfaced in logs with reason codes. Testing: - Unit tests added and passing locally - Integration suite run against a staging dedicated cluster (stable) - Manual canary on production with 10 fleets for 48h (metrics sampled and compared) Rollout: Start with opt-in via config for customer-facing dedicated fleets. After monitoring for 72h across canaries, flip default to enabled for new customers and schedule migrations for existing fleets over 4 weeks. Related: ENG-10021 implements operator-side rollout primitives used here. SUP-4521 is the customer support ticket that motivated immediate hotpatch behavior. Reviewer notes: See review conversation for design questions and PR feedback. CI: All checks passed (unit, integration, lint, fmt). Merge: Squash-merged to main after signoff and green CI.
